course_description: This course provides a foundation in dental public health and professionalism in the practice of dentistry. The course explores principles of behaviour management in clinical care. Professional matters such as ethics, governance and regulation of dental practice in Australia will also be covered. The competency building activities of this course will provide students with learning through workshops and a series of case-based learning.

course_aims: This course aims to provide students with an understanding of communication skills, health law and ethics, inter-professional practice and information literacy.

learning_outcomes.description: Describe patient’s rights to health care and explain complaint mechanisms at practitioner and governance level.
Explain principles of responsible communication and professional use of media.
Reflect on the importance of practising with personal and professional integrity, honesty, and trustworthiness.
Analyse and make judgements on scenarios which involve patients' consent, confidentiality, and autonomy.
Apply the policies of the regulatory bodies that govern the provision of oral health services in Australia.
Critically apply the ethical principles and legal responsibilities underpinning the provision of dental care.

assessment_details.title: Ethical Scenario VLOG
assessment_details.task_description: Students will be presented with a choice of five ethical scenarios. Each student is required to individually produce a reflective response that thoughtfully engages with the scenario selected. The reflection must integrate relevant ethical concepts, theories, and frameworks discussed in class. The submission format should be a video. Students may optionally use a PowerPoint presentation to accompany their reflection. Read full task description Hide full task description

learning_activities.topic: Week 1 :27/07/2026-02/08/2026: Dentistry in Australia Topic 1: Dentistry in Australia A description of the profession of dentistry within Australia and defining professionalism. Learning outcomes: L03, L05

Week 2: 03/08/2026-09/08/2026: What is Bioethics? Topic 2: What is bioethics? The ethical principles involved with dentistry and how they help inform professional practice. Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06

Week 3: 10/08/2026-16/08/2026: Regulation, AHPRA and Dental Board Topic 3: Regulation, AHPRA and Dental Board An introduction to the legal system and laws that impact dentistry. Accessing and understanding regulations Learning outcomes: L01, L05

Topic 4: Negligence, deception and conflict of interest Topic 4: Negligence, deception and conflict of interest Legal framework for negligence and compensation under Australian laws and risk management principles. Explores paternalistic and non-paternalistic deception. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

Week 6: 31/08/2026-06/09/2026: Autonomy, Consent and Confidentiality Topic 5: Autonomy, consent and confidentiality Exploring the key concepts of autonomy, consent and confidentiality including ethical and legal considerations. Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06

Week 7: 07/09/2026-13/09/2026: Ethical issues in practice Topic 6: Ethical issues in practice Scope of practice, standard of care, duty to treat and terminating a patient/dentist relationship. Learning outcomes: L01, L05, L06
Week 8: 14/09/2026-20/09/2026: Quality control Topic 7: Quality control Evaluation of quality control: self and others. Mandatory reporting and whistle blowing. Learning outcomes: L05, L06
Week 09: 21/09/2026-27/09/2026: Ensuring Practitioner Health Topic 8: Ensuring practitioner health Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04
Week 11: 12/10/2026-18/10/2026: Dentistry as a business Topic 11: Dentistry as a business Business ethics versus professional ethics. Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L06

Week 12: 19/10/2026-25/10/2026: Expanding scope of dental practice Topic 12: Expanding scope of dental practice Evidence-based practice: ethics of differences in opinion versus differences in science. Learning outcomes: L04, L06
